reason: Dormant read path only, Part 1a of the note tier (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-21-note-tier-design.md 5.1/5.2). Adds nora/language/note_render.py (render_notes + NOTES_BLOCK_NOTE), TagContext.notes defaulted to (), and _notes_block in nora/agent/prefill.py, wired into the volatile tail immediately after <facts> and before <group_transcript> - both are workspace-keyed rather than room-keyed, so they sit together at the wide end of the widening-scope order, settled before open. The block renders the INDEX: one line per standing note carrying title and description only, never the body (which arrives through note_read, 5.2) and never the closing condition (the spec fixes the line's contents at title+description in 5.1 and again in 6.2, and Note.closing_condition carries no length cap, so rendering it would mean either unbounded per-tag text or a render-time truncation that nora/domain/notes.py deliberately moved into the constructor). The index is uncapped by decision: no top-N, no elision, no relevance scoring, because a note missing from it is invisible to her and invisible is indistinguishable from absent - the prompt budget is paid by TITLE_MAX_CHARS/DESCRIPTION_MAX_CHARS in the domain type and by the curator's retirement pass, and a named test with sixty notes turns red if a cap is ever added. A retired note never renders. Carries its own block note rather than ROOM_BLOCK_NOTE for the same reason <facts> does - 'distilled from this room's own messages' is false for a workspace-keyed block - plus one clause no sibling needs, that each line is a pointer and not the content. Nothing writes TagContext.notes yet, so every deployed prompt renders no <notes> block at all and gains no tokens; no schema change, no tool, no behaviour a user can observe.
